_comment: Cities (src/engine/cities.py). Every Kestrian settlement is a living city with population, local morale and a
construction queue (one project at a time, paid for up front).
population: starting population by settlement type (x 0.85..1.15, seeded).
local morale: each week moves `morale_pull` of the way toward the national civil morale plus local factors
(morale_factors). A city below unrest_below costs the nation unrest_morale civil morale a week.
buildings: cost (CR), weeks to build, max per city, and effects:
hospital  - outbreaks start here only outbreak_factor as often, the disease reaches it only spread_factor as
often, and local morale is higher;
bunker    - Kestrian formations within `radius` rows fight with at least `fortification` (as a trench line);
local_industry - +1 to the national pool of military factories when finished.
news: local headlines. Each week a city may print one; the most urgent situation picks the pool.

hospital.name: Hospital
hospital.description: Isolation wards, a laboratory and trained staff. Epidemics rarely start or spread here.

bunker.name: Bunker Complex
bunker.description: Reinforced-concrete strongpoints, cellars and tank traps: defenders fight as if entrenched.

local_industry.name: Local Industry
local_industry.description: A new munitions works: +1 military factory for the national war economy.

battle_near: Citizens report hearing artillery throughout the night; panic buying at local markets.
Ambulance trains unload at {city} station hour after hour. The schools have become field hospitals.
Windows rattle in {city} as the guns fire all night. Refugees from the front fill the churches.
Military police close the road east of {city}. Wounded men sleep on the station platforms.
Artillery heard in the distance; rolling blackouts implemented city-wide.
Air raid sirens sound for the third time this week. Shelters at capacity.
Refugees flood the central plaza; military cordons established to maintain order.
enemy_near: Vosk scouts reported in the woods outside {city}; the home guard digs trenches in the parks.
Blackout strictly enforced in {city}. Rumours of enemy tanks beyond the river unsettle the town.
{city} evacuates its children west as the front draws closer.
infected: Mass graves dug outside city limits as quarantine fails.
{disease} spreads through the tenements of {city}; the undertakers cannot keep up.
Doctors in {city} beg for disinfectant and clean water as {disease} cases double in a week.
Churches in {city} ring the passing bell every hour. {disease} fills the fever wards.
Hospitals overwhelmed; military police enforce strict street curfews.
Mass graves expanded outside city limits. Local authorities urge calm.
Pharmacies looted overnight. Ministry of Health issues stark warning.
quarantined: Troops and nurses seal the infected districts of {city}; delousing stations work around the clock.
Quarantine holds in {city}: new {disease} cases fall for the first time in weeks.
Quarantine lines hold, but citizens report smell of burning from southern wards.
blockaded: Enemy warships off {city}: the harbour is empty, dockers idle, bread queues lengthen.
Not a single merchantman has entered {city} this week. Coffee and sugar vanish from the shops.
Harbor master reports all civilian shipping halted. Docks stand eerily silent.
Fish markets empty. Foreign cargo ships refuse to break the Vosk naval line.
Panic buying at grocers as import shipments fail to arrive for second week.
disaster: Survivors still being dug from the rubble around {city}. The railway will not run for weeks.
Relief kitchens feed thousands in {city} after the disaster. Engineers promise the line within the month.
construction: Scaffolding rises over {city}: work on the new {building} goes on through the night.
{city} council celebrates as foundations are laid for a new {building}.
City center paralyzed by Ministry of Infrastructure heavy machinery.
Local unions protest 16-hour shifts required for state construction projects.
Citizens complain of deafening drilling as state project breaks ground.
completed: The new {building} in {city} opens its doors. Crowds cheer the Lord Protector's name.
Ribbon cut on {city}'s new {building}; the mayor calls it 'a fortress for the future.'
winter: Coal ration cut again in {city}. Families burn furniture to stay warm.
Frozen pipes burst across {city}; queues for water at the fire hydrants.
low_morale: Angry crowds outside {city} town hall demand bread and an end to the war.
Anti-war slogans painted overnight on the walls of {city}. Police make arrests.
Munitions workers in {city} walk out after another cut to the bread ration.
high_morale: Steelworker quotas exceeded; patriotic parades in the town square.
{city} oversubscribes its war-bond quota by half. Bunting on every street.
Volunteers queue around the block at the {city} recruiting office.
A brass band plays in {city} market square as the harvest comes in early.
quiet: Life goes on in {city}: the trams run, the cinemas are full, the war feels far away.
{city} newspaper prints the week's casualty lists. The cafés are quieter than they were.
Allotments dug in every park in {city} as the 'Grow for Victory' campaign takes hold.
Women take over the {city} tram depot as the men go to the front.
Local steel quotas met; Mayor declares public holiday.
Minor protests over ration cards dispersed by civil police.
Train schedules delayed due to troop movements at Central Station.
Cinema attendance up 12% as government releases new war newsreels.
Black market prices for coffee and sugar hit record highs.
